nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers with every $a_i$ positive. If $U_1, \dots, U_n$ are subgroups of $G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$, and $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ are elements such that the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint, then $a$ is $G$-harmonic.
nodes.title: Constructing a G-harmonic tuple

nodes.summary: For every group $G$, the empty tuple of natural numbers is (vacuously) $G$-harmonic.
nodes.title: The empty tuple is G-harmonic

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. Then $a$ is $G$-harmonic if and only if every $a_i$ is positive and there are subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.title: Characterization of G-harmonic tuples

nodes.summary: For every group $G$, the one-entry tuple $(1)$ is $G$-harmonic; the subgroup $G$ itself, of index $1$, with coset representative $1$ witnesses this.
nodes.title: The tuple (1) is G-harmonic

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. The tuple $a$ is $G$-harmonic if every $a_i$ is positive and there exist subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.title: G-harmonic tuples

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers has $a_i = 0$ for some $i$, then $a$ is not $G$-harmonic.
nodes.title: Tuples with a zero entry are not G-harmonic

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers is $G$-harmonic, then $a_i > 0$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Entries of a G-harmonic tuple are positive

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers is $G$-harmonic, then there exist subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.title: Witnesses for a G-harmonic tuple

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
